story.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Flagged for Extremism Concerns Before Incident
story.summary: A FlyDubai co-pilot, who wielded an axe during a flight, had previously been flagged for extremism concerns. This incident has raised questions regarding the airline's employee vetting processes and how the co-pilot was allowed to operate a flight with Israeli passengers, given Israel's stringent security measures.

timeline_highlights.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Attacked Captain with Axe, Barred from Flying Over Extremism Concerns
timeline_highlights.summary: The co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight to Israel, identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain with an axe in what UAE officials describe as an attempted terrorist act. Al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying in Oman due to concerns over extremist views. The incident has raised alarms within the aviation industry, already struggling from recent crises.
key_facts: Hamam al-Hammami attacked the captain with an axe.
The incident occurred on a FlyDubai flight to Israel.
Al-Hammami was barred from flying in Oman due to extremism concerns.

The elections are marked by the significant presence of a pro-Russian politician and ongoing ethnic tensions, alongside concerns regarding the stalled European Union membership bid.

related_stories.title: Cornell President Responds to Alleged Gang Rape Incident at Fraternity
related_stories.summary: Cornell University's president, Michael Kotlikoff, described the allegations of a gang rape involving a student at a fraternity house as 'deeply disturbing.' In a recent video statement, he emphasized the need for the university to improve its response to such incidents. The allegations have led to increased scrutiny of the university's handling of sexual assault cases, with the accuser, identified as Jane Doe, suing the university and several former students.

related_stories.title: Understanding the Kelvin Wave Impacting Sea Levels on the West Coast
related_stories.summary: A Kelvin wave is currently affecting sea levels along the West Coast, characterized by bulges of water that raise sea levels as they travel. Unlike tsunamis, these waves do not crash onto the shore but rather resemble water sloshing in a bathtub. This phenomenon is significant for coastal areas as it can lead to temporary increases in sea level.
